name: (2019 QC4)
assessment: Traveling at over 47,000 km/h, this 120-meter rock poses no immediate threat as it maintains a safe distance of 19 million kilometers from Earth. It remains a standard celestial passerby that provides more of a scientific observation opportunity than a planetary risk.

name: (2016 RT17)
assessment: This moderately sized 117-meter asteroid is cruising through the void at a relatively leisurely 32,154 km/h. Passing nearly 27 million kilometers away, it remains well beyond any orbital resonance that would cause concern for our home planet.

name: (2007 DK8)
assessment: This massive near-kilometer-wide behemoth is tearing through space at a blistering 83,613 km/h. Despite its intimidating size and velocity, its trajectory keeps it a comfortable 47 million kilometers away, far outside the danger zone.
